# Lapa Electric selects Fingerprints for India’s first biometrics-enabled e-scooter

Fingerprint Cards AB

2 min read

* [FGRRF](/quote/FGRRF/ "FGRRF")

[![Fingerprint Cards AB](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///ywAAAAAAQABAAACAUwAOw==)](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/0955c7dbabee5199debae20260bb34c46b88ac3ee4ec5f2b1a452efb5b2e5240/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fglobenewswire.com%2F3da8ea991f848976d6a6ebbcf2077e46)

Fingerprint Cards AB

 

[Fingerprint Cards AB](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=hwZ278tEpVIN1X1_ta-kCeSOrIT-Bs1JfADwOtyzxZZ1UEzL8VgvfehYaD2SSIqjLKEdefP5Emoa8yBBJyeFhDszhnzrS3v2kdiy9q_eaWHHpqVDo4wyQXmBUk6ALJ7jdrqhBv8vgBjwW7VK_u1FpCSIO7UzTbe95tw5K-VkSABFFLfUhTJUVwk6Ql1Hso94) (Fingerprints™), has partnered with [Lapa Electric](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=JboloKHijO8BHN6MGXaob_RWYPKmhIGWwdlRSAwehJ6U24INCX3Lbd7CRJ1w1Krh8x_-TIVmYmldNe6ek-sryQ==), an Indian-based premium electric mobility start up, to create India's first biometric-enabled electric scooter (e-scooter) to bring in the best every security system into two wheelers.

The use of e-scooters in India has sky-rocketed in recent years, and this growth is expected to continue. In 2023, the [penetration rate](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=TBq7SQmCHB90uiKj3AWhkPFntj9ZNNzMy8zvEEMW4wYy6xkwp4YcPkuAQjkjt5nGp8GfxoftlK-wfg61GSMIGydjKPv1p6ibo-AYYkHvl91Jgvw4vITg3JDs5A4L1NQ0-w5l6ale6LYHuACju0gl2S1Jzjmp0686veLovlbLCs8=) of e-scooters in India was 13%, yet by 2030 this is projected to grow to 75%.

Adam Philpott, CEO of Fingerprints comments: "Over the last 10 years, biometrics has become the preferred authentication method for consumers and businesses alike. From our phones, laptops, and payment cards to our homes and workplaces, biometrics is adding security while removing friction. As our lives, and our vehicles, become increasingly connected, we must enhance security processes and biometrics is a natural progression to underpin the future of mobility."

By replacing traditional physical keys with biometric authentication, only enrolled users will be able to use the e-scooter, drastically reducing the risk of theft. In addition, users won't have to worry about losing or having their keys stolen anymore as they become the key.

Pavan Kumar at Lapa Electric adds: "At Lapa Electric we are in the verge of bringing in a totally new engineering approach to E two wheelers like for example replacing heavy steel chassis with weddings and bolts and nuts with light and robust seamless monocoque carbon fiber chassis. Now we're replacing physical keys with biometric smartness. The resulting scooter embodies premium and performance."

Though the idea of having a biometric sensor was brilliant, but the challenge was to find the smallest sensors that can be integrated into our patented console and throttle system. Here is where the collaboration of engineering between Fingerprints and Lapa took birth.

Lapa Electric's e-scooter will integrate Fingerprints' proven biometric sensor and algorithm. The biometric-enabled e-scooters are presently under vehicle road testing will be launched in limited numbers by early next year.

Learn more about how biometric authentication can strengthen physical and logical access control, while improving convenience for consumers [here](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=9e1zWhAUGpgx_jqgFys9genxlMjC7szz6guayiMCSV78VbIog8IKq5Yi8ckHWlv4J4PKz2icYzyBRIxatom9LEWh0yaANdr12HrtTza30U91hl2YlrxAqWYdf4NHcBwXEjOCLzC_LdgRtulyM-9qYjJoVfs4V4A6ZR_1nIuzBhPS_8DStO7oQrDwHP9CTPgq).

# Predictive Maintenance for Fleets: Preventing Downtime with Smart Technology

By oxmaint on February 27, 2026

![predictive-maintenance-fleets-smart-technology](./manage-post-2k26/uploads/predictive-maintenance-fleets-smart-technology.png)

Every fleet manager knows the sinking feeling. A driver calls in from the highway: engine warning light, smoke from under the hood, a truck loaded with time-sensitive deliveries now sitting dead on the shoulder. The tow truck is an hour away. The customer is already on the phone. The repair bill will be steep, but the real damage is the cascade of missed routes, reshuffled schedules, and eroded trust. This scenario plays out thousands of times daily across fleets worldwide, and in most cases, the failure was preventable. Predictive maintenance uses real-time vehicle data, sensor intelligence, and machine learning to catch these problems weeks before they strand a truck. In a market projected to reach $122 billion by 2035, fleet operators who embrace smart maintenance technology are pulling ahead while those stuck in reactive mode fall further behind. Ready to stop reacting and start predicting? [Sign up for OxMaint](https://app.oxmaint.ai) and take the first step.

## What Predictive Maintenance Actually Means for Fleets

Predictive maintenance is fundamentally different from both reactive maintenance (fixing things after they break) and preventive maintenance (servicing on a fixed schedule regardless of need). In fleet operations, predictive maintenance continuously monitors vehicle health through telematics, IoT sensors, and onboard diagnostics to detect the early warning signs of component failure. It then uses data analytics and machine learning algorithms to forecast when a specific part or system is likely to fail, giving fleet managers a precise window to schedule repairs at the lowest cost and disruption.

The distinction matters because fleets do not age evenly. Two identical trucks in the same fleet can have vastly different maintenance needs depending on their routes, loads, driver behavior, and environmental conditions. A calendar-based service schedule treats them identically, which means one gets serviced too early while the other develops a hidden problem between intervals. Predictive maintenance closes that gap by responding to what is actually happening inside each vehicle, not what a manual says should happen.

## Leveraging Fleet Telematics to Improve Maintenance Workflows

If you’re like most fleet managers, you probably associate fleet telematics solutions with location tracking. Though telematics devices are great for monitoring vehicle location (especially when your fleet is spread out), there are many more benefits to leveraging fleet telematics.

Fleet telematics devices provide a mass amount of vehicle data, including information on the health status of your vehicles, making them an ideal resource for tracking and analyzing your fleet. Receiving vehicle data from your telematics device is a great way to improve your fleet maintenance plan.

> By supplementing telematics data with fleet management software, fleet managers can receive [real-time telematics data](https://www.fleetio.com/blog/gain-complete-fleet-visibility-with-telematics-integrations) in a cloud-based platform to automate maintenance workflows and immediately address vehicle issues as they arise.

Housing all fleet data on a comprehensive platform ensures managers have maximum visibility into vehicle status, maintenance schedules and inspection results to prevent vehicle downtime and improve fleet efficiency. Here are a few ways pairing a telematics device with fleet management software can improve your fleet maintenance process.

## 1. Improve Fleet Operations by Receiving Real-Time Data

When your fleet is spread out across the map, receiving up-to-date vehicle information can be difficult. Drivers may not be able to easily communicate while on the road, and if you’re still relying on paperwork to manage your fleet, you could be waiting days or weeks to receive pertinent data.

> Fleet technology eliminates communication gaps and provides you with real-time data regarding your assets.

A fleet telematics system can provide real-time data regarding the health of your vehicle to keep you informed of any issues and make necessary fleet maintenance decisions to avoid downtime.

Integrating a telematics system into fleet management software provides increased visibility into overall operations, allowing you to automate fleet maintenance processes and make data-driven decisions regarding your assets.

While telematics tools can provide real-time vehicle information, fleet management software centralizes all of your fleet data to automate workflows and keep you connected with your team. By pairing the two, fleet managers can accurately monitor driver behavior, fleet maintenance, fault alerts and overall vehicle health.

## 2. Conduct Preventive Maintenance Based on Odometer Readings

Most fleets base their [preventive maintenance (PM) schedules](https://www.fleetio.com/manage/features/pm-scheduling) on mileage, but manually tracking odometer readings is inefficient and often error-prone. Paper-based systems don’t provide fleet managers with accurate, real-time updates to ensure PM tasks are carried out on time.

By utilizing fleet telematics devices, odometer readings can be automatically uploaded into fleet management software, ensuring managers have an organized way to manage fleet maintenance and never fall behind on PM tasks.

> Fleet managers can set service reminders in fleet management software based on odometer readings.

Setting service reminders and due-soon thresholds allows you and your team to receive email or push notifications to schedule preventive maintenance.

Integrating a telematics device into your software system ensures accurate odometer readings are uploaded each day. You can also sync updates from any of your assets at any time with one click to get instant updates from your fleet telematics system.

Instead of manually tracking odometer readings and calculating when fleet maintenance is due, software automates these processes by pulling current telematics data to ensure your fleet maintains a proactive PM schedule.

## 3. Immediately Address Issues from Diagnostic Trouble Codes

When it comes to unplanned maintenance, time is of the essence. Vehicle issues can fester under the hood for days, weeks, even months at a time without you knowing, resulting in more extensive and costly repairs.

While that check engine light may go ignored by drivers, fleet managers can gain peace of mind and create fleet maintenance strategies based on information from their telematics tools. By pairing a telematics system with fleet management software, fleet managers receive instant notification of diagnostic trouble codes (DTC) across their fleets.

> DTC and fault alerts from your telematics devices can be linked to mobile work orders in fleet management software, providing maintenance technicians a complete picture of any issues.

Linking DTC alerts directly to line items issues are addressed and are automatically recorded in your fleet’s service history, ensuring you and your team have accurate insight into a vehicle's current and past condition.

Some assets trigger multiple fault alerts, and determining which alerts are relevant can disrupt your day. [Fleetio](https://www.fleetio.com/blog/4-ways-fleet-telematics-can-help-you-manage-maintenance) allows managers to choose which alerts they receive, ensuring only relevant alerts come to your inbox.

Pairing your telematics system with fleet management software allows you to see issues across your assets immediately and jumpstart the maintenance process to reduce overall downtime. Fleetio also maintains a report of all DTCs, allowing you to spot possible maintenance trends across your fleet and proactively manage them.

## 4. Aggregate Fleet Maintenance and Telematics Data into Configurable Reports

To maintain an efficient fleet, fleet managers must track and analyze every aspect of their operations. Fleets who still rely on paper and spreadsheets to manage operations have a difficult time compiling fleet data and accessing relevant information quickly.

> Managing your entire fleet with cloud-based software ensures all of your data is organized into easy-to-read visualizations.

With configurable fleet reports, fleet managers can analyze the exact data they need to make the best decisions for their fleet.

Tracking maintenance and telematics data in fleet management software eliminates manual data entry, saving fleet managers countless hours and allowing them to use that extra time to analyze data and monitor their operations.

By integrating telematics data into fleet software, users can view maintenance reports regarding asset utilization, service history and fault codes. Fleet management software also calculates cost-per-mile based on geolocation data, allowing you to monitor fleet expenses and develop strategies to cut costs and improve your bottom line.

### India's EV two-wheeler sales crossed 1.27 million units in 2025, with monthly volumes holding above 100,000.

India's [electric two wheeler market](https://www.rideapart.com/news/category/electric-motorcycles/?utm_campaign=yahoo-feed) has just crossed a new threshold. Monthly wholesale dispatches are now holding above 100,000 units, and full year 2025 retail sales cleared roughly 1.27 million electric scooters and motorcycles.

And here's the twist: startups lit the fire, and now the legacy giants are running the table. Once buyers got curious about electric, they didn't necessarily stay loyal to the disruptors. They gravitated toward brands they already trusted. When daily transportation is on the line, familiarity matters. And in India, trust plus scale is a powerful combo.

For a while, it looked like pure EV brands would dominate India's scooter future. Companies like [Ola Electric](https://www.rideapart.com/ola-electric/?utm_campaign=yahoo-feed) and [Ather Energy](https://www.rideapart.com/news/703524/ather-450-apex-electric-scooter/?utm_campaign=yahoo-feed) were the poster children of the transition. Fast forward to 2025 and the leaderboard tells a different story. It's the old guard that has muscled its way to the top.

[![TVS To Ramp Up Production Of iQube Electric Scooter](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///ywAAAAAAQABAAACAUwAOw==)](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/f909c6c2ed5011e90e12a7fcd839fa4b34d6fbb17602634fd798cd3945315b11/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Frideapart_articles_415%2Fed6fbb6cf4836ab31e4dd145b8f7ab9c)

TVS To Ramp Up Production Of iQube Electric Scooter

 

In fact, TVS Motor Company is now the volume king. The [iQube](https://www.rideapart.com/news/660305/tvs-iqube-750percent-sales-growth-india/?utm_campaign=yahoo-feed) alone moved around 298,000 units in 2025, giving TVS roughly a quarter of the entire electric two wheeler market. That's not a niche play. That's scale. And that also means that TVS is having the time of its life right now with the recent launch of the [BMW F 450 GS](https://www.rideapart.com/news/784176/2026-bmw-f-450-gs-coming-very-soon/?utm_campaign=yahoo-feed) which it co-developed, as well as the resurgence of [Norton Motorcycles](https://www.rideapart.com/news/777973/norton-atlas-manx-eicma-video/?utm_campaign=yahoo-feed) which it now owns.

Right behind it sits Bajaj Auto with the electric Chetak, clocking more than 260,000 units for the year. Bajaj leaned hard on its dealer network and brand trust, and it worked. Buyers who might have hesitated on a startup badge clearly felt more comfortable going electric with a name they've known for decades.

Ather Energy is still very much in the fight. Its Rizta helped push the brand north of 150,000 units in 2025. That's serious volume for a company that started as a tech driven challenger. Meanwhile, Hero MotoCorp and its Vida sub brand cleared more than 110,000 units, making it one of the fastest growing players in the space.

[![2024 Bajaj Chetak Electric Scooter Gets Tech And Performance Enhancements](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///ywAAAAAAQABAAACAUwAOw==)](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/d6efa0970219e44dd3b80d1ef3a7d774b3f7de2a1a4b611e35c49e90a66473cf/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Frideapart_articles_415%2F31a0401d1e27c854cf10102d03d239f2)

2024 Bajaj Chetak Electric Scooter Gets Tech And Performance Enhancements

 

Then there's Ola Electric. Once the headline grabbing leader, it has slipped down the rankings even as the overall market expanded. It still sells meaningful numbers, but the momentum has clearly shifted.

All of this adds up to more than bragging rights. India sold over 1.27 million electric two wheelers in 2025 alone. Monthly dispatches staying above 100,000 units shows the supply chain and demand curve have stabilized. This is no longer a subsidy spike story. It's a structural shift.

For the rest of the world, this matters because India is one of the [largest two wheeler markets on Earth](https://www.rideapart.com/features/783569/india-20-million-motorcycles-sold-2025/?utm_campaign=yahoo-feed). Unlike the US or much of Europe, [scooters](https://www.rideapart.com/news/category/scooters/?utm_campaign=yahoo-feed) in India are not lifestyle toys. They're daily transportation. When that segment electrifies at scale, it changes manufacturing priorities, battery sourcing, and platform development worldwide.

China still dominates the electric two wheeler universe in sheer numbers, but India is now firmly in heavyweight territory. And the biggest takeaway is clear. The transition to electric is happening, and the legacy manufacturers are proving they can adapt just as fast as the disruptors.

# Fleet Telematics: Turn Alert Signals Into Maintenance Action

Telematics tells you what's happening. Maintenance software determines what happens next (or it better). Here's how fleets turn DTC faults, mileage and location data into maintenance action.

### What you need to know about fleet telematics

1. **Telematics captures the signal. Maintenance software creates the outcome:** GPS data, DTC faults and mileage readings only become valuable when they trigger maintenance action.
2. **The biggest challenge isn't collecting data:** Most fleets already have the telematics data they need. The opportunity lies in turning that data into work orders, preventive maintenance and more informed maintenance decisions.
3. **Integration determines ROI:** Connecting telematics with fleet maintenance software helps teams prioritize repairs, improve preventive maintenance compliance and keep assets on the road longer.

---

Most fleets have more telematics data than they know what to do with. Assets constantly report their location, DTC faults keep rolling in and odometer readings update automatically without lifting a finger. Collecting the data isn't the challenge anymore. Turning it into maintenance action is.

Telematics captures the signal. Maintenance software is what turns that signal into work that actually gets done. Every maintenance outcome starts with a signal, but only fleets that act on those signals truly capture the full value of telematics.

Closing that gap starts with understanding what telematics actually captures, where the signal stalls and what it takes to turn it into real maintenance work. That's where a [fleet optimization platform](https://www.fleetio.com/solutions/fleet-management-software) comes into play.

## What Is Fleet Telematics?

Fleet telematics is like a smoke alarm. It can tell you something needs attention, but it won't put out the fire for you. Behind that alert is a relatively straightforward system. Fleet telematics combines GPS, asset diagnostics and a wireless data connection to continuously collect operational data from your assets. A device wired into the engine control module — or an OEM-native connection on newer assets — captures location, speed, odometer readings, DTC faults, and driver behavior signals such as harsh braking and excessive idling. That data then travels over a cellular or satellite network before landing in a telematics platform.

In practice, telematics helps fleet managers:

* Know where every asset is at any moment
* Coach drivers when harsh braking and idling spike
* Catch a fault code before it grounds an asset
* Tie odometer data to preventive maintenance schedules
* Hold the line on Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) and Department of Transportation (DOT) compliance
* Cut fuel waste linked to bad routing

But every one of those use cases depends on something happening after the data arrives. The telematics platform captures the signal. But if it doesn’t convert into maintenance work, what’s the point?

## Alerts Can’t Turn a Wrench

The signal itself is rarely the bottleneck. Most fleets running 50 assets or more already have a telematics provider, and many run more than one after acquisitions, vehicle-type splits or shifting contracts. The constraint sits between an alert firing and the work it should trigger.

A [diagnostic trouble code](https://www.fleetio.com/glossary-of-fleet-terms/diagnostic-trouble-code) (DTC) on a service van earns its keep only when it reaches a technician with enough context to prioritize the repair. A milestone odometer reading is just another data point until it triggers a preventive maintenance (PM) task that lands on a tech's calendar with parts and instructions attached. Location data answers "where is this asset right now" almost everywhere. The harder question is what the maintenance team should do because of where the asset is.

That gap is where the value of telematics either compounds or evaporates. A fleet with telematics but no maintenance system to act on the data ends up paying for instrumentation that never moves the work forward (or adds more work to your plate). The dashboards look pretty to leadership, but they produce nothing in the shop. A DTC fires on a service van Friday afternoon, nobody triages it over the weekend, and the van rolls Monday morning into a roadside breakdown that costs ten times what a scheduled repair would have been. A PM threshold passes because the last odometer reading was entered manually three weeks ago, and now the fleet is out of compliance on an asset everyone assumed was covered. And we could go on and on.

## Three Handoffs That Close the Gap

Closing that gap is a maintenance software job, and it involves three concrete handoffs.

### 1. DTCs become work orders

When a fault triggers in an asset wired to a Geotab or Samsara device, the alert flows into Fleetio with the asset, the code, the timestamp and the related history. Fleetio links that alert to a [digital work order](https://www.fleetio.com/features/digital-work-orders) with the right parts, photos and assignee, so a technician picks up a ready-to-execute task.

Fault Rules let a manager classify each code in advance, with options to ignore low-signal alerts or flag critical ones, so an inbox of telematics-fed faults arrives already prioritized. Fleetio's [Faults Summary report](https://help.fleetio.com/en_US/faults-overview) rolls up those alerts across asset groups, so a manager can see whether the same code is appearing across a class of assets before it cascades into unplanned downtime.

###### Pro Tip

DTC faults create value only when they become maintenance work. Automatically routing them into digital work orders helps technicians spend less time chasing alerts and more time resolving issues.

### 2. Odometer readings become PM schedules

Telematics integrations automatically log mileage, so PM compliance stops depending on whether a driver remembered to enter a reading at the pump. Service thresholds tied to mileage trigger work without the manual chase.

[Town of Apex](https://www.fleetio.com/resources/case-studies/apex), North Carolina, manages 400 vehicles plus 230 pieces of equipment to serve 80,000 residents, the kind of fleet where tracking PM schedules manually across that many assets is a losing game. After centralizing on Fleetio with a Geotab integration, the town achieved a 17% year-over-year decrease in total operating costs while consistently meeting an 80% preventive maintenance compliance target. The difference came from automated mileage data feeding directly into PM schedules and the procurement decisions the team could make once all the maintenance data lived in one place.

### 3. Inspections plus telematics become a single asset record

Failed Driver Vehicle Inspection Report (DVIR) items are converted directly into work orders in [Fleetio Go](https://www.fleetio.com/go), with photos, parts and assignees attached. When that record sits next to telematics-fed odometer history, fault codes and location pings, the technician working the repair has the full operational picture in one place.

[Boyle Transportation](https://www.fleetio.com/resources/case-studies/boyle-transportation), a national trucking company that handles security-sensitive materials for life sciences and defense clients, runs its Samsara telematics in Fleetio for automated odometer updates, DTC alerts and location tracking on the same dashboard. Fleet Maintenance Supervisor Ernest Acevedo describes the workflow this way: "Fleetio makes up 40 percent of what I do. I plan my day based on the Fleetio dashboard." His team saves around 30 minutes per technician daily through Fleetio Go, time that used to go to manually coordinating between telematics alerts and repair workflows.

Fleetio is extending that signal-to-action loop further with [AI Service Advisor](https://www.fleetio.com/ai), currently in open beta. It prioritizes issues by operational risk, flags exceptions on repair orders, and routes the telematics faults that need attention first.

## One Maintenance System, Any Telematics Stack

Closing the gap on a single asset with one telematics provider is one thing. Most fleets are not single-provider shops. After an acquisition, a contract change or a pilot program, a typical operation ends up with one telematics provider on the trucks, another on the trailers, partial coverage on the equipment and no telematics on the spares. The integration design lets a fleet add a provider, swap one out or run mixed coverage without rebuilding the maintenance system underneath.

[JW Danforth](https://www.fleetio.com/resources/case-studies/jw-danforth), a mechanical contractor founded in 1884 with 170-plus assets across HVAC, plumbing, piping and building electrical controls work, runs Fleetio with a Geotab integration. # From Data to Action: How Predictive Maintenance Reduces Costs and Technical Downtime in Fleet Management

In a competitive context such as **corporate mobility**, every minute of vehicle downtime represents a tangible cost: service delays, operational inefficiencies, and reputational damage. In this scenario, predictive maintenance – enabled by **telematics data** – becomes a strategic ally for **fleets**, transforming vehicle management from reactive to truly proactive.

Until a few years ago, fleets mainly relied on **reactive maintenance models** (intervening only after a breakdown) or preventive ones (following fixed maintenance intervals). Both approaches have clear limitations: the former exposes fleets to the risk of sudden failures, while the latter may generate unnecessary costs. **Predictive maintenance**, on the other hand, uses real-time data analysis to anticipate the emergence of problems. Thanks to telematics, parameters such as mileage, component temperature, abnormal vibrations, driving styles, and ECU error codes are collected, analyzed, and transformed into operational insights.

The added value of telematics solutions lies in the integration between onboard devices, **analytical platforms**, and connected services. The data collected from vehicles is processed by predictive algorithms that identify risk patterns and generate timely alerts for fleet managers. This enables the advance planning of interventions to avoid critical failures; reduce extraordinary maintenance costs; extend vehicle lifespan; and optimize **Total Cost of Ownership** (TCO).

Imagine a corporate vehicle starting to show a steady increase in vibration on an axle, detected by telematics sensors. The system interprets the data as an early sign of wear and alerts the fleet manager of the potential risk. Thanks to this warning, the technical intervention can be scheduled in advance, avoiding a breakdown that would have resulted in vehicle downtime, towing, and temporary replacement.

Investing in predictive maintenance is not just a technological choice, but a lever for improving operational efficiency. The return on investment is measured by: reduction of unplanned downtime; decrease in extraordinary repair costs; improvement in overall fleet reliability; and greater satisfaction for drivers and end customers. According to industry analysis, companies adopting predictive maintenance models can reduce downtime by up to 30% and maintenance costs by up to 20%.

Fleet managers, drivers, workshops, and client companies all benefit from a more efficient ecosystem, with vehicles always operational, more reliable planning, and fewer unforeseen events. But the advantage is also reputational: those who invest in predictive technologies demonstrate attention to sustainability, safety, and innovation.

Telematics has ushered in a new era in **fleet management**. It is not just about collecting data, but about transforming it into value.
